subject: Nasty bug in hoverId and clickId of plotOutput()?

messages.author: 889de486273d901d
messages.subject: Nasty bug in hoverId and clickId of plotOutput()?
parts:
I think I have run across a bad bug in the new hoverId and clickId functionality for plotOutput() introduced in v0.7.0.
Can anyone else confirm?   Anyone know of a workaround?

The documentation for plotOutput says, "The value will be NULL if the user is not hovering, and a named list or vector with x and y elements indicating the mouse position in user units."
As far as I can tell, that is true only for the first plot you make.   All subsequent hover or click events are reported in the user coordinates of that first plot!   
The system never resets the coordinate system.   

Live demo: http://spark.rstudio.com/cswarth/testhover

Source code: https://gist.github.com/cswarth/6678546

Run locally:   shiny::runGist("https://gist.github.com/cswarth/6678546")

- chris

messages.subject: Re: Nasty bug in hoverId and clickId of plotOutput()?
parts: You may want to look into Highstock. It is based on Highcharts, has similar API plus navigation bar and data grouping. Data grouping is used for aggregating close data points to increase performance. I am using Highstock for financial time-series, but it should work for scatter plots as well.
